findings.claim: Tropos in Acid stands level on rock that falls away under its front half toward the puddle. The front of the cabinet overhangs a slope of about 9 degrees. Both front feet are in the air and the back feet are sunk 25 mm into the rock.
findings.evidence: The speaker is at (0,0), rotate_z -8. Fitted z is -0.025: the top-front edge step falls on the projected row within 1 px at 9.4 px/cm (ov-acid-topleft.jpg, ov-acid-topright.jpg). That equals settle()'s highest ray hit, 0.000 at the back corners, minus the 0.025 sink. The ground is acid_rain_el.wet_ground. Its flat r 0.7 zeroes the lumps, but _lumps applies the dips everywhere: dip (0,-0.95) r 1.1 depth 0.2 and dip (-0.2,-1.2) r 1.2 depth 0.2. Mesh height under each foot, before the render-time displace of 0.07 (+/-35 mm): back-left 0.000, back-right 0.000, front-left -0.047, front-right -0.065. The foot bottoms are at -0.025, so the back feet are 25 mm into the rock and the front feet are 22 mm and 40 mm above it (the front-right one clears even the largest displacement). Along the front-bottom edge (z -0.013) the rock mesh is at -0.049 to -0.080, a gap of 36-67 mm that closes to zero near mid-depth. The slope is 7-10 degrees front to back and 2 degrees across. The five settle hits were 0.000, 0.000, -0.052, -0.071 and -0.014. The picture confirms this ground: the computed waterline (mesh at the puddle's z of -0.11, 9 cm in front of the front face) sits exactly on the rendered shoreline (acid-wateredge-check.jpg). The front-right foot (stem and swivel base) is plainly visible hanging under the cabinet's corner over lit rock. At the site's 1200 px a dark band about 30 px tall runs under the left two-thirds of the front edge where the rock drops away. On the 360 px home tile it is about 9 px and reads as shadow. Crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b109/habitats/acid-evidence-full-res.jpg and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b109/habitats/acid-evidence-site-size-x2.jpg (cyan: the cabinet's bottom; red: the rock under its front edge; yellow dashed: where rock meets the bottom; magenta: the front-foot gaps), and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b109/habitats/acid-site-clean-x3.jpg (clean, site size). Fix: keep the dips out of the footprint, either by applying the flat-zone factor to the dips or by giving dip 1 a radius that ends at the front face, so the rock under all four feet is level with a lip at the front face. Then re-render. No earlier note on this in the record.

findings.picture: All eight habitats (the cause of H1). Code: spinoffs/barkhorn/biomes/habitat.py settle() on r48-biomes
findings.claim: settle() lowers the speaker until its lowest foot meets the highest of five downward ray hits: the four corners of the feet-base bounding box (+/-0.25, -0.209/+0.201) and its centre. It never checks how far apart the hits are. On any uneven ground the downhill feet are left in the air, with no warning.
findings.evidence: In Acid the hits spread 71 mm and passed silently. The other seven passed only because their ground is level by construction inside a flat zone: Ember r 0.45, Dust 2.2, Poison and Fog 0.9, Haze 0.8, Ice 2.6, Smoke 0.9. The rays also see whatever mesh lies under the corners (drift triangles, scatters), which is how Ice ended up 19 mm high (H4). Suggest: fail the shot when max hit minus min hit exceeds about 5 mm, and cast the rays at the foot centres.

findings.claim: Tropos in Ember is sunk into solid lava crust. Its feet are 18 mm below the crust's surface and the cabinet's bottom panel is 6 mm below it. findings.evidence: Fitted z is -0.018, exactly as expected (top edge on the projected row, 9.4 px/cm; ov-ember-topleft.jpg). ember_el.terrain is level at z 0 within r 0.45: relief, ropes and lobes are multiplied by level=0, and the nearest lava channel stays at least 0.81 m from the feet, beyond its 0.76 m reach. So all four feet are on level crust, bedded 18 mm, with the crust displaced +/-15 mm (displace 0.03). The bottom edge meets the crust with no gap and no foot shows (ov-ember-base.jpg). The same bedding applies elsewhere, all on soft ground and all invisible: Dust 28 mm in sand (cabinet 16 mm in), Poison 20 mm in leaf litter (8 mm), Haze, Fog and Smoke 12 mm in soil (cabinet bottom at the surface).
